args.old_string: 6. Only after all public tests pass and the algorithm has a clear correctness argument, call `submit` exactly once. Then stop.
args.new_string: 6. Add a hidden-test defense gate before submission. Passing the samples is not evidence of correctness: for any nontrivial or hard problem, use at least one remaining `run_python` call to do one of the following: compare the proposed algorithm with an obviously correct brute-force/enumeration solver on many small random and exhaustive edge cases, or construct a direct independent checker for the key invariant. Also test boundary-sized shapes and hostile patterns suggested by the constraints (duplicates, equal values, empty/one-element transitions, maximum indices, disconnected/degenerate cases, and worst-case inputs). If this finds a mismatch, fix the derivation—not just the example—and rerun public tests plus the checker. Explicitly recheck common silent errors: 0/1-based and k-th-position conventions, inclusive interval endpoints and subtree ranges, operation order/state used for costs, all legal target values (including zero), signed versus unsigned/large integer arithmetic, and whether a claimed monotonicity or convexity actually holds. For a performance-sensitive solution, benchmark a realistic maximum-size input and account for Python allocation and repeated sorting; an algorithm that only passes tiny samples is not acceptable. Only after this gate, all public tests pass, and the algorithm has a clear correctness argument, call `submit` exactly once. Then stop.
